description: The first READ reports '22' - a duplicate key - and delivers a record with it, and the record is still not displayed. This is the sharpest statement of what guards the DISPLAY at app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl:78: the test at :77 is IF END-OF-FILE = 'N', not 'if a record came back'. The read arm at :101 moves 12 into APPL-RESULT, the guard chain reaches :113 PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM, and control never returns to the mainline - so the record that was moved into the CARD-RECORD area by READ ... INTO at :93 is simply never written out. A translation that displayed whatever the read handed back, or that treated a delivered record as success, would emit a 150-character line here that the COBOL does not. '22' is reachable only through the alternate-index path in this estate, and CBACT02C browses the base cluster, so the status is induced by the test's own stub - which is exactly what a case is for when the seeded data cannot reach an arm. The arm itself is real: :101 catches every status other than '00' and '10'.

expectedMessages.text: START OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT02C
